parole.significato: A flat piece of coarse material used for wiping one’s feet, or as a decorative or protective floor covering.
parole.testo: Inherited from Middle English matte (“mat”), from Old English meatte (“mat”), from Late Latin matta (“mat made of rushes”), from Punic or Phoenician (compare Hebrew מיטה \ מִטָּה (mitá, “bed, couch”)). Cognate with German Matte (“mat”), Danish måtte (“mat”), Faroese and Icelandic motta (“rug, mat”),

parole.significato: One of the chief magistrates who ruled ancient Carthage.
parole.testo: From Latin suffes, from Late Punic 𐤔𐤐𐤈 (špṭ, “judge”). Doublet of shophet.
